audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings tell the player to hold Defiant Dance (W) to eat Lillia's poke and to tank her R wake-up hit. Riot's text says Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage; Lillia's whole kit is magic, with true damage on the edge of Blooming Blows. Blooming Blows' true-damage edge is never mentioned, so the page's repeated 'shred her resists' advice points at the wrong stat. Swirlseed's behaviour — it keeps rolling until it hits a wall — is never stated, and Lilting Lullaby's cooldown never appears.
audit.why: Charging W against Lillia is a two-second commitment that mitigates nothing and leaves you standing in her Dream Dust. The true-damage edge is also why hugging her body is better than trading at max Q range.
audit.corrected: All three Defiant Dance claims replaced; Blooming Blows' true-damage edge written into whys[3]; Lilting Lullaby's 110s rank-3 cooldown added to spikes[3]; Swirlseed's roll-until-wall behaviour added to early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the packet and with the page's own whys. Level 1 read Lillia while whys[0] says neither of you wins it; Level 2 read Skill while the packet gives it to Irelia; Level 6 read Lillia while whys[4] and spikes[1] both call it your premier all-in window; 2+ items read Irelia while whys[6] says she reclaims the game.
audit.why: The Level 6 row was the damaging one — the page told the reader in prose that 6 is her kill window and in the chart that it belongs to Lillia, on a 55.96% matchup.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 4 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group; Level 1 rating raised to 5/10, Level 6 to 7/10, 2+ items dropped to 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike is described without a cooldown, so 'trade around Blooming Blows' has no timing attached — and Blooming Blows is on 4 seconds at rank 5, which is not something you wait out at all.
audit.why: The real punishable cooldowns here are Swirlseed at a flat 12s and Lilting Lullaby at 110-150s. Telling the player to track a 4-second ability as the matchup-defining cooldown is misdirection.
audit.corrected: R's cooldown written into spikes[3]; Swirlseed's flat 12s written into early as the actual poke window to step into.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] writes the ability as 'Blooming Blow'.
audit.why: Riot's name is Blooming Blows, plural. The packet flagged it as a probable wrong name and the kit file confirms.

edits.before: W (Defiant Dance) gives you the damage-reduction channel to eat her DOT poke and survive into your level-3 spike.
edits.after: Level 2 is yours: Defiant Dance won't blunt her magic poke, so win it by denying CS and stacking passive into level 3.

edits.before: Your Bladesurge passive comes online and cooldowns tighten — at max stacks you shred her resists and out-skirmish a Lillia who can only kite, not duel.
edits.after: Your passive comes online and cooldowns tighten — you out-skirmish a Lillia who can only kite, but armour won't save you: the edge of Blooming Blows is true damage.

edits.before: Past 2 items full-AP Lillia kites fights with R sleep and Q speed — she chips with passive DOT poke and dodges your melee. Close the lane before her teamfight scaling outweighs your dueling edge.
edits.after: Past 2 items full-AP Lillia kites with Q speed and Lilting Lullaby sleep — 110 seconds at rank 3, so the window right after she spends it is your only one. Close the lane before her scaling outweighs your duel.

edits.before: Use W (Defiant Dance) to tank her R-sleep wake-up hit and ride out her passive DOT, then re-engage with reset Q
edits.after: Break her sleep early with a hit of your own — Defiant Dance is physical-only and does nothing about the wake-up damage

edits.before: Stack Q (Blooming Blow) movement speed to kite at range, spacing so your Bladesurge dash and E-stun never connect
edits.after: Stack Blooming Blows (Q) movement speed to kite, spacing so your Bladesurge dash and E-stun never connect

edits.before: Level 1 is even — you only have Q, so farm with Bladesurge resets off the wave and don't chase her Q-spin poke into a bad spot, since her passive DOT keeps ticking after she runs. The moment you hit 3 the lane flips: E (Flawless Duet) is your first stun, and crucially Lillia has no dash to break it — so when she steps up to last-hit or commits to a Q spin, drop the blades to clamp her, stun, then Q-reset before she can ramp her movement speed away. Don't whiff E into open ground — her whole game is using Q speed to dance just outside your dash range, and a missed E lets her free-poke you with Swirlseed slow and DOT.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — you only have Q, so farm Bladesurge resets off the wave and don't chase her spin into a bad spot, since her passive damage keeps ticking long after she has run away. The moment you hit 3 the lane flips: E (Flawless Duet) is your first stun and Lillia has no dash to break it — so when she steps up to last-hit or commits to a spin, drop the blades to clamp her, stun, then Q-reset before her movement speed ramps out of range. Swirlseed is a flat 12 seconds and keeps rolling until it hits a wall, so step in on the miss and never take a trade with a wall at your back.

edits.before: This is your window. With your Bladesurge passive online and cooldowns tightening, every E-stun chains into Q-resets off the minions and at max stacks your passive shreds her squishy resists fast. At 6, R (Vanguard's Edge) is the hard answer to her Q-speed kiting — wall the lane behind her so when you E-stun she can't run the ramp out, then run her down. Hold W (Defiant Dance) for her R-sleep: tank the wake-up hit through the damage reduction and keep tunneling. Force these fights now while you flatly out-duel a Lillia who hasn't scaled and can only kite, not trade blow-for-blow.
edits.after: This is your window. With your Bladesurge passive online and cooldowns tightening, every E-stun chains into Q-resets off the minions and your on-hit melts a squishy Lillia fast. At 6, R (Vanguard's Edge) is the hard answer to her Q-speed kiting — wall the lane behind her so when you E-stun she can't run the ramp out, then run her down. Don't save Defiant Dance for her R-sleep either; it cuts physical damage only, so break the sleep early with a hit instead. Force these fights now while you flatly out-duel a Lillia who can kite but cannot trade blow-for-blow.

notes: Three strings told the player to soak Lillia's damage with Defiant Dance, which reduces physical damage only — Lillia deals magic plus a true-damage edge on Blooming Blows. That true-damage edge also invalidates the page's repeated 'shred her resists' framing. Four chart rows were inverted against the packet and the page's own prose, including Level 6, where the prose calls it your premier all-in and the chart gave it to Lillia; flipped as a matched group. 'Blooming Blow' corrected to Blooming Blows.
